survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Uruguay using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The document describes that PISA provides mean estimates with uncertainty (95% confidence intervals) and that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard issues (asterisk), implying complex survey design handling in the underlying OECD database computations. The factsheet itself does not specify the exact student weight variable(s) (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the specific weighting implementation cannot be extracted from the text provided. Analysts using the OECD PISA database should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate procedures as implemented in the database tables referenced (e.g., I.B1.* and II.B1.*) to obtain correct standard errors for means and proportions.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Uruguay factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Uruguay performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time. It reports that average performance in mathematics was down versus 2018, about the same in reading, and up in science; over 2012–2022, reading and science improved slightly while mathematics returned to lower levels last seen in 2012. In 2022, 43% of students reached at least Level 2 in mathematics (OECD average: 69%), 59% in reading (OECD average: 74%), and 59% in science (OECD average: 76%), with top-performer shares of 1% (math) and 2% (reading and science). The factsheet also highlights within-country gaps: socioeconomic status predicts mathematics performance and accounts for 18% of variation in Uruguay, and boys outperform girls in mathematics while girls outperform boys in reading. Methodologically, the document is descriptive and does not present an ML modeling pipeline, PV-combining procedure, or missing-data strategy in the text; it relies on OECD PISA database tables for uncertainty estimates and quality standards.
